initial_scene: The robot stands beside a white tabletop. A pointed metal garden trowel with a wooden handle lies above a narrow rectangular tray; the blade points toward the window. Both hands initially hang down. The source initial PNG was viewed at native 320 by 568 display resolution after full-sequence inspection.

observed_sequence.action: Initial pause with trowel resting on the tabletop and both hands lowered.
The far, window-side right arm rises and extends over the tabletop; the right hand reaches the wooden handle and closes around it. The foreground left hand stays down.
observed_sequence.confidence: high for grasp action; medium for anatomical naming

observed_sequence.action: The right hand lifts the trowel clear of the tabletop, holding the handle while the metal blade projects outward. By frame 202 it is visibly suspended.
The right wrist tips the blade downward and the arm carries it over the tray, lowering the blade into its open interior. Native frames 228, 266 and 280 establish the blade orientation and entry.

The right hand moves the blade along the length of the tray in a scooping stroke. The tray remains stationary without help from the other hand. No distinct soil or other picked-up material is visible.
observed_sequence.confidence: high for stroke; medium for exact bottom contact

observed_sequence.action: The right hand raises the trowel out of the tray and rotates the blade back toward a more horizontal orientation. Native frames 376 and 400 show it clear of the tray.

The right arm returns the trowel to the tabletop above/beside the tray, lowering it with the blade pointing toward the window. Native frames 432 and 450 show the tool resting on the surface while the hand remains at the handle.
The right hand opens away from the handle and withdraws toward the body. The released trowel remains on the tabletop; the left arm remains lowered and does not touch the tool or tray.

arm_hand_roles.right: Active far/window-side arm: reaches for and grasps the wooden handle, lifts the trowel, rotates and lowers its blade into the tray, performs the scooping stroke, lifts it out, returns and releases it on the table, then withdraws.
arm_hand_roles.left: Near/foreground arm remains lowered throughout; no stabilization, transfer or object contact is observed.
arm_hand_roles.coordination: One-hand tool manipulation only. No hand-to-hand transfer or interaction with a person occurs; the tray is unsupported by either hand.

anatomical_side_evidence.convention: Robot-relative sides established from the visor/front-of-head and anterior torso facing the table, together with the two shoulder/arm attachment paths. The foreground descending arm attaches to the nearer left side; the active arm extends from the opposite, window-side right shoulder.
anatomical_side_evidence.limitation: The oblique elevated side view and torso/shoulder overlap partly obscure the active upper-arm attachment. The anatomical designation is supported by body orientation rather than screen left/right alone; the original publisher-linked description also calls the active hand right, but was not used to replace visual inspection.

terminal_state: The trowel lies released on the tabletop beside the tray, blade directed toward the window. The active right hand has withdrawn from its handle. The tray remains in place and no carried material or gardening result is visible. The left hand remains lowered.
uncertainties: The active right shoulder is partly occluded in this oblique view, so anatomical naming has medium confidence; the active arm is unambiguously the far/window-side arm.
The tray looks empty at this resolution. Blade movement within it is visible, but exact bottom contact and movement of any fine material cannot be resolved; no soil pickup or transfer is asserted.
annotation_discrepancies: The broad gallery instruction describes outdoor gardening tasks; the visible clip is a tabletop trowel scooping demonstration with no visible outdoor work or material transfer. The publisher-linked detailed description of right-hand pickup and a scooping motion in a container matches the motion observed.
selected_execution_status_basis: The observable tool-use cycle completes: grasp, lift, blade entry and scooping stroke in the tray, lift out, return to table, release and withdrawal. This status does not assert an unseen gardening or material-transfer result.

inspection_coverage.media_preserved: Entire original source MP4 and source PNG remain byte unchanged.

world_model_prompt: The humanoid robot grasps the garden trowel's wooden handle with its right hand and lifts it from the tabletop. It lowers the blade into the rectangular tray, makes a scooping stroke along the tray, and lifts the trowel back out. It returns the trowel to the tabletop beside the tray, releases the handle, and draws its right hand back. Keep the camera fixed; preserve robot geometry, physically valid joint motion, and normal gripper opening and closing.
